definitionEn: a fighter in a small, independent armed group that attacks a stronger official army
situation: People take up arms and fight in small, mobile groups against a much stronger government or army, rather than in open, direct battles.

examples.text: For years, [[guerrillas]] hiding in the mountains ambushed government patrols and then vanished into the forest.
During the civil war, thousands of young farmers joined the [[guerrillas]] hiding in the hills.
The documentary follows a former [[guerrilla]] who now works as a peace negotiator in the same region.

texts: The rebels relied on classic [[guerrilla]] tactics, striking fast and disappearing before help arrived.
Small business owners sometimes joke about using [[guerrilla]] marketing to compete with big brands on a tiny budget.
The activists organised a [[guerrilla]] campaign of surprise protests outside the company's offices.

badCollocation.text: The country declared [[guerrilla]] on its enemy.
badCollocation.noteRu: «Объявить партизанскую войну» — to declare guerrilla warfare/war. Само слово guerrilla не используется как объект declare без warfare.

collocationTask.prompt: the rebels waged a ___ war against government forces
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Партизанская война» — guerrilla war/warfare. Rebellion, revolution и insurrection — существительные, не сочетаются как определение перед war.

nuance.text: The [[guerrillas]] avoided open battles, striking government convoys by surprise and retreating into the jungle.
nuance.explanationRu: Guerrilla — боец нерегулярных отрядов, воюющий внезапными нападениями, избегая открытого боя. Rebel — шире: любой, кто восстаёт против власти, необязательно партизанскими методами.

reverse.text: The student [[rebels]] simply refused to attend classes until their demands were met.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь нет вооружённой борьбы — это мирный протест, поэтому rebels, а не guerrillas, которые воюют исподтишка с оружием в руках.

fixIt.text: The [[soldiers]] hid in the jungle for years, ambushing government convoys and then melting back into the forest, always avoiding open battle.
fixIt.explanationRu: Обычные soldiers сражаются в составе регулярной армии открыто; здесь описана многолетняя партизанская война из засад — это guerrillas.

reply.context: A friend texts you: "I just started reading a novel about a small group fighting a much bigger army in the jungle."
options: That sounds interesting! Is it about guerrillas fighting against a much stronger army?
Guerrillas? I thought that was a type of gorilla you find in Africa!
I am not familiar with the term guerrilla; kindly elaborate on its precise definition.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ уместен и по теме. Во втором guerrilla перепутан с gorilla (горилла) — частая ошибка. Третий звучит слишком официально для сообщения другу.

definitionEn: official advice or instructions that help you decide what to do
senseNote: Здесь — официальные указания/рекомендации от органа или эксперта (guidance from the ministry), а не просто дружеский совет по жизни.
situation: An authority, expert or institution provides official advice or instructions to help people make the right decision or follow the correct procedure.

examples.text: The ministry issued new [[guidance]] on how schools should handle bullying complaints.
Her academic advisor gave her useful [[guidance]] on which modules to choose next year.
The government's official [[guidance]] recommends staying home if you have flu symptoms.

texts: New employees receive detailed [[guidance]] on company policies during their first week.
The pamphlet offers simple [[guidance]] for parents worried about screen time.
Doctors welcomed the update, since the previous [[guidance]] on the vaccine was confusing.

badCollocation.text: Please [[guidance]] me through this application form.
badCollocation.noteRu: Guidance — существительное; глагол «направлять, консультировать» — to guide: please guide me through this form.

collocationTask.prompt: The new staff handbook provides clear ___ on health and safety
collocationTask.explanationRu: Существительное — guidance: provides guidance on. Guide, guiding и guided — другие формы, они не подходят после clear в этой конструкции.

nuance.text: The council's official [[guidance]] on recycling was updated last month, and all households must now follow it.
nuance.explanationRu: Guidance — официальные указания от организации, которым часто нужно следовать. Advice — более личный, необязательный совет; «official advice that everyone must follow» звучит нелогично.

reverse.text: My grandmother always gives me the best [[advice]] about relationships, even though she's never been on a dating app.
reverse.explanationRu: Личный, неформальный совет от близкого человека — это advice, а не guidance, которое звучит слишком официально для семейного разговора.

fixIt.text: The health department published new [[orders]] recommending that people wear masks indoors during flu season.
fixIt.explanationRu: Orders — обязательные приказы, а «recommending» подразумевает необязательность; для необязательных официальных рекомендаций нужно guidance.

wordFormation.text: The retired teacher now works as a career [[guidance]] counsellor at a local college.

reply.context: A classmate texts you the night before an important scholarship interview: "I have no idea what to expect tomorrow, I'm so nervous."
options: Why not email your professor tonight? She always gives such helpful guidance before interviews.
Don't worry, I'll give you guidance tomorrow morning so you're not late.
Relax, it's just an interview, stop overthinking everything.
reply.explanationRu: Первый вариант уместен: просить совет у преподавателя. Во втором guidance перепутан с «показать дорогу». Третий слишком резкий и не поддерживает друга.

rewrite.original: A counsellor explained which universities might suit my grades and interests.
rewrite.frame: A counsellor gave me ____ on which universities might suit my grades and interests.

definitionEn: the fact of having done something wrong or committed a crime
senseNote: Здесь — юридический факт вины (guilt or innocence), а не чувство вины — более базовое значение слова (feeling guilty).
situation: A court, jury or investigation must decide whether a person actually committed the crime they are accused of.

examples.text: The jury took only two hours to reach a verdict on the defendant's [[guilt]].
Without solid evidence, prosecutors struggled to prove [[guilt]] beyond reasonable doubt.
She always maintained her innocence, but new DNA evidence eventually confirmed her [[guilt]].

texts: The letter he left behind seemed to be a clear admission of [[guilt]].
Refusing to answer questions can sometimes look like an admission of [[guilt]], even if you are innocent.
New witnesses came forward, adding to the mounting evidence of his [[guilt]].

badCollocation.text: He was sentenced to [[guilt]] of five years.
badCollocation.noteRu: Срок дают не «вине», а по приговору: he was sentenced to five years (in prison); guilt — сам факт виновности, у него нет «срока».

collocationTask.prompt: New evidence was enough to establish his ___ beyond doubt
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое сочетание — establish someone's guilt. Guiltiness, wrongness и culpableness звучат неестественно в этом контексте.

nuance.text: Even after the trial confirmed his [[guilt]], he refused to apologise to the victims.
nuance.explanationRu: Guilt — официально установленный судом факт виновности; blame — более общее «вина/ответственность» в бытовом смысле: «the trial confirmed his blame» звучит странно.

reverse.text: Everyone at the office quietly put the [[blame]] on the new intern, even though nothing was ever proven.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь нет суда и доказательств — обычное «переложить вину» в разговоре, поэтому blame, а не формальное guilt.

fixIt.text: After a two-week trial, the court finally confirmed his [[blame]] and sentenced him to three years.
fixIt.explanationRu: После суда используют формальное guilt (виновность), а не бытовое blame — приговор подтверждает именно guilt.

wordFormation.text: Even though nobody blamed him, he couldn't shake off a nagging sense of [[guilt]] after the accident.

reply.context: A friend says: "The trial finally ended today after six long weeks."
options: Really? Did the jury find enough evidence of his guilt, or was he cleared?
That's such a relief — I felt so much guilt watching it drag on for weeks!
Lol finally, that trial was dragging forever, who cares who did it.
reply.explanationRu: В первом guilt — юридический факт вины, к месту после суда. Во втором guilt перепутан с чувством неловкости. Третий слишком развязный для темы суда.

rewrite.original: The evidence was strong enough to show that she had committed the fraud.
rewrite.frame: The evidence was strong enough to establish her ____.

definitionEn: an instinctive feeling about something that is not based on facts or clear thinking
senseNote: Здесь — интуиция, инстинктивное чувство (a gut feeling), а не желудок/живот — более базовое значение слова.
situation: You sense that something is true or that you should act in a certain way, even though you cannot explain the reasons logically.

examples.text: Something in my [[gut]] told me not to sign the contract, and I was right to listen.
Ignore the spreadsheets for a moment — what does your [[gut]] say about this investment?
He's not the analytical type — he makes every major decision by following his [[gut]].

texts: Sometimes you just have to trust your [[gut]] and make the call.
Her [[gut]] told her something was off about the deal, even though the numbers looked fine.
When in doubt, I usually go with my [[gut]] rather than overanalysing everything.

badCollocation.text: I felt it with my [[gut]] sense.
badCollocation.noteRu: «Нутром чувствовать» — a gut feeling или to feel something in your gut; «gut sense» так не говорят.

collocationTask.prompt: She had a ___ feeling that something was wrong
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение — a gut feeling. Stomach, belly и tummy — тоже «живот», но с feeling так не говорят.

nuance.text: He couldn't explain it with numbers or facts — he simply trusted his [[gut]].
nuance.explanationRu: Gut — интуитивное чувство без логических оснований; здесь прямо сказано, что решение не основано на фактах, поэтому logic (логика) сюда не подходит.

reverse.text: The engineers double-checked every measurement, relying purely on [[logic]] and hard data rather than guesswork.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь описан точный расчёт, а не интуиция, поэтому logic, а не gut.

fixIt.text: I can't really explain why, but my [[brain]] just told me not to trust him, and I was right.
fixIt.explanationRu: Brain/mind — логическое мышление, а «не могу объяснить, почему» указывает на интуицию, то есть gut, а не brain.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Should I take the safer job offer or the risky startup one? I've made a list of every pro and con."
options: Honestly, forget the list for a second — what does your gut say?
Your gut has been bothering you lately? Maybe you should see a doctor.
Just pick one already, why are you even asking me.
reply.explanationRu: В первом gut — интуиция при выборе. Во втором gut перепутан с желудком (жалоба на здоровье). Третий слишком резкий и не помогает другу.

rewrite.original: Without any real proof, she just sensed that he was hiding something.
rewrite.frame: Her ____ told her he was hiding something.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Нутром почувствовала» = her gut told her / she went with her gut feeling.

definitionEn: to secretly get into a computer system without permission, often to steal or damage information
senseNote: Здесь — взламывать компьютерную систему; более старое значение — грубо разрубать (to hack through something) — не тренируем.
situation: Someone secretly breaks into a computer system or network without permission, usually to steal data or cause damage.

examples.text: A teenager managed to [[hack]] the airline's booking system from his bedroom computer.
Investigators believe a rival company paid someone to [[hack]] their servers and steal designs.
Within hours, activists had [[hacked]] the ministry's website and replaced the homepage with a protest message.

texts: It's surprisingly easy to [[hack]] a smart fridge that still uses the factory password.
The group claims it can [[hack]] almost any home security camera within minutes.
Students in the coding club learned, under supervision, how someone might try to [[hack]] a school network.

badCollocation.text: Someone [[hacked]] my wallet and took all my cash.
badCollocation.noteRu: Hack — про компьютеры, аккаунты и сети; кошелёк просто «украли» (steal from) или «обчистили», а не hacked.

collocationTask.prompt: Someone managed to ___ into the hospital's patient database
collocationTask.explanationRu: Про компьютерные системы говорят hack into. Invade, trespass и infest с базами данных так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: It took the security team days to figure out how the intruders had [[hacked]] the entire network, not just one password.
nuance.explanationRu: Hack — получить незаконный доступ к системе/сети в целом; crack — конкретно взломать код, пароль или шифр. Здесь речь о всей сети, поэтому hack, а не crack.

reverse.text: It only took the software a few seconds to [[crack]] the four-digit PIN code.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь взламывают один конкретный код, а не систему целиком, поэтому crack, а не hack.

fixIt.text: Someone [[stole]] into the company's servers overnight and copied thousands of customer records.
fixIt.explanationRu: Stole into — тихо прокрасться куда-то физически; для взлома компьютерной системы нужно hacked into.

wordFormation.text: The conference invited several former [[hackers]] to speak about cybersecurity.

reply.context: A colleague says: "Our company website went down for six hours yesterday, and now customer data seems to be missing."
options: That sounds serious — do they think someone managed to hack the site?
Weird, maybe someone just hacked their arm trying to fix the cables under the desk.
lol probably just a glitch, IT will sort it eventually, don't stress.
reply.explanationRu: В первом hack — взлом системы, к месту. Во втором hack перепутан со старым значением «рубить». Третий слишком небрежный для утечки данных.

rewrite.original: An unknown attacker broke into the university's network and stole exam papers.
rewrite.frame: An unknown attacker ____ the university's network and stole exam papers.

definitionEn: to publicly praise someone or something as very good or important
senseNote: Здесь — «провозглашать, превозносить» (hailed as a hero); базовые значения — «окликнуть такси» и «град (осадки)» — не тренируем.
situation: The media, critics or the public publicly describe a person, event or achievement as excellent, important or successful.

examples.text: Critics [[hailed]] the film as one of the finest dramas of the decade.
The new vaccine was [[hailed]] as a breakthrough that could save millions of lives.
Local newspapers [[hailed]] her as a hero after she pulled two children from the icy lake.

texts: The peace agreement was [[hailed]] as a historic achievement by leaders on both sides.
Reviewers [[hailed]] her debut novel as the most original book of the year.
The coach was [[hailed]] as a genius after the team's surprise championship win.

badCollocation.text: My friends just [[hailed]] my new haircut, they said it looked nice.
badCollocation.noteRu: Hail — торжественно провозглашать выдающимся (hailed as a hero/masterpiece); для лёгкой похвалы стрижки нужно просто compliment/praise.

collocationTask.prompt: The peace deal was ___ as a turning point in the region's history
collocationTask.explanationRu: В переносном значении «провозглашать историческим» — to hail. Shouted, called out, yelled — буквально «кричать», сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: World leaders [[hailed]] the ceasefire as a major diplomatic success.
nuance.explanationRu: Hail — восторженно, публично провозглашать успехом; greet — просто отреагировать на новость, без обязательной высокой оценки. «Greeted as a major success» звучит слабее.

reverse.text: Most employees simply [[greeted]] the new dress code policy with a shrug.
reverse.explanationRu: Реакция здесь равнодушная (пожали плечами), а hailed предполагает восторженную похвалу — это не подходит.

fixIt.text: The scientists [[announced]] the discovery as the most important breakthrough in a decade.
fixIt.explanationRu: Announce — просто сообщить факт; оценочное «провозгласить чем-то великим» — hailed (as).

reply.context: A colleague says: "Did you see? The mayor's new transport plan just got announced."
options: Yes, and interestingly, local papers have already hailed it as a game-changer for the city.
Really? I hope it doesn't hail during the announcement, the forecast looked bad.
Meh, politicians always say stuff like that, whatever.
reply.explanationRu: В первом hail — «провозглашать успехом», уместно. Во втором hail перепутан с градом (осадками). Третий слишком небрежный.

rewrite.original: Newspapers described the young pianist as a genius after her first concert.
rewrite.frame: Newspapers ____ the young pianist as a genius after her first concert.

definitionEn: to some extent, but not completely
senseNote: Здесь — «отчасти, частично» (meet somebody halfway = пойти на уступки); базовое значение — «на полпути, посередине пути» — не тренируем.
situation: Something happens only to a limited degree, or two sides both make some concessions so neither gets everything they wanted.

examples.text: After a long negotiation, the union agreed to meet management [[halfway]] on the pay rise.
I only believe him [[halfway]] — his stories always sound a little too perfect.
The film is only [[halfway]] convincing; the plot has some good twists but weak characters.

texts: You'll have to meet me [[halfway]] if you want this deal to work.
She was only [[halfway]] joking when she said she might quit.
The company met the protesters [[halfway]], agreeing to some but not all of their demands.

badCollocation.text: [[Halfway]] the class agreed with the new policy.
badCollocation.noteRu: Halfway — это «отчасти, частично», а не «половина (чего-то)»: «половина класса» — half the class, без -way.

collocationTask.prompt: You need to meet your business partner ___ if you want the deal to succeed
collocationTask.explanationRu: Идиома — meet somebody halfway (пойти на уступки). Average, central и balanced в этой конструкции не используются.

nuance.text: I trust him [[halfway]] at best — I always double-check what he tells me.
nuance.explanationRu: Halfway — только отчасти, не полностью; completely (полностью) противоречит смыслу «всегда перепроверяю» — доверие явно неполное.

reverse.text: After years of working together, she trusts her business partner [[completely]], with no need to double-check anything.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь доверие полное (не нужно перепроверять), поэтому completely, а не halfway.

fixIt.text: We couldn't agree on the price, so we decided to meet [[midway]] and both accept a small loss.
fixIt.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение — meet somebody halfway. Midway здесь не используется, хотя по смыслу похоже.

reply.context: Your roommate says: "I think we should split the rent 70/30 since I have the bigger room, but you want 50/50."
options: How about we meet halfway and do 60/40 instead?
Sure, my new apartment is halfway between the subway and the bus stop, so it's convenient either way.
No way, 50/50 or I'm moving out.
reply.explanationRu: В первом halfway — компромисс. Во втором halfway использовано буквально, не по теме. Третий слишком резкий, без компромисса.

rewrite.original: Neither side got everything they wanted, but both accepted a partial compromise.
rewrite.frame: Both sides agreed to meet each other ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Пойти на уступки» = meet each other halfway.

definitionEn: to stop moving or happening, or to make something do this
situation: A process, activity or movement that was continuing suddenly stops, often because of a decision or an unexpected problem.

examples.text: The government ordered construction to [[halt]] immediately after cracks appeared in the bridge.
Heavy snow [[halted]] traffic across the entire region for several hours.
Doctors managed to [[halt]] the spread of the infection before it reached other wards.

texts: A sudden strike could [[halt]] production at the factory within days.
The referee had to [[halt]] the match when fans ran onto the pitch.
New sanctions are designed to [[halt]] the country's nuclear programme.

badCollocation.text: The company decided to [[halt]] its employees for being late.
badCollocation.noteRu: Halt — остановить процесс или движение (halt production/talks), а не человека за проступок: сотрудника можно punish/discipline, но не halt.

collocationTask.prompt: Torrential rain forced organisers to ___ the outdoor concert less than an hour in
collocationTask.explanationRu: Мероприятие прерывают/останавливают — halt. Arrest — «арестовать» (человека), freeze — «заморозить», postpone — «перенести», это не то же самое.

nuance.text: Organisers decided to [[halt]] the race after the storm hit, hoping to restart it once conditions improved.
nuance.explanationRu: Halt — временно остановить процесс, который может возобновиться; cancel — отменить полностью. Здесь явно планируют restart, поэтому halt, а не cancel.

reverse.text: Because of the storm, organisers had to [[cancel]] the race entirely; there was no chance to reschedule it that season.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь гонка не возобновится вообще — это полная отмена, cancel, а не временная остановка halt.

fixIt.text: Because of the leak, engineers had to [[cancel]] the machine immediately to prevent an explosion, and restarted it an hour later once it was safe.
fixIt.explanationRu: Машину не «отменяют» (cancel — про мероприятия/заказы), а halt — временно останавливают; здесь она позже снова заработала.

wordFormation.text: His [[halting]] explanation made it clear he hadn't prepared for the meeting.

reply.context: A coworker says: "Why has the delivery truck been sitting outside for twenty minutes?"
options: Apparently there's a burst pipe, so the building manager had to halt all deliveries until it's fixed.
Maybe the driver is just having a halt for lunch.
Deliveries have been provisionally suspended pending resolution of the aforementioned plumbing malfunction.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ уместен: halt — приостановить процесс. Во втором halt использован как «привал», не по теме. Третий звучит слишком официально.

rewrite.original: The strike forced the factory to stop all production for three days.
rewrite.frame: The strike forced the factory to ____ all production for three days.
